1.explanation: This minimal example uses Grommet’s Meter (type="circle") and a button that changes its value.  In Chrome, because Grommet’s styled component applies `transition: all 300ms` to the arc’s <path>, updating the value causes the entire path geometry to animate—even its radius—producing the strange expanding/shrinking effect.  You can paste this into a fresh Create-React-App (or codesandbox.io) with grommet@2.3.1 to see the bug reproduce exactly as in the original report.
1.bug_scenario: When you update the value of a circle-type Meter in Chrome, the SVG <path> that draws the arc has a `transition: all 300ms` applied to it.  Because “all” properties are being transitioned, the path’s underlying geometry (its bounding box, radius, etc.) gets interpolated—resulting in the weird “ghost path” and janky animation seen in the screenshot.  (In Firefox/Safari they don’t transit all properties the same way, so you see no glitch there.)
